external_sources.bounded_support: Vitest 4 migration removes environmentMatchGlobs and directs users to projects.

independent_review_field_correction.smallest_correction: For installed Vitest 4, use projects. Retain historical syntax only with its verified applicable version range, and follow the installed version documentation for other versions. Have the example follow the existing installed-version check.
independent_review_field_correction.reason: The retrieved primary source verifies Vitest4; do not extrapolate an unverified future 4+ range.

findings.synthesis_smallest_correction: For installed Vitest 4, use projects. Retain historical syntax only with its verified applicable version range, and follow the installed version documentation for other versions. Have the example follow the existing installed-version check.

findings.title: Purpose and README overstate experiment execution
findings.consequence: A user can reasonably expect this auto-invocable designer to execute an experiment; the concrete artifact and workflow specify design and analysis, not production assignment or metric collection.
findings.smallest_correction: Say designs and analyzes experiments in Purpose and README; make execution a separately authorized implementation/operations handoff. Treat this as ambiguous capability wording, not proof an experiment was run.
findings.behavioral_claim: No live behavioral evaluation was run; this finding concerns the shipped text/fixture contract.
findings.independent_review_qualification: Purpose/README capability overstatement relative to the design/readout contract. No experiment execution or unauthorized action was observed.

findings.title: Live incident callers route to an authoring-only skill
findings.details:
`incident-response-runbook` describes its job as document authorship and explicitly excludes live diagnosis. Its Stop Conditions route live work to the existing runbook and `systematic-debugger`; its own trigger case selects the debugger for a current failure. In contrast, the backup verifier's trigger case for a corrupted production database and failed checkout selects `incident-response-runbook`, and the cloud baseline reviewer hands suspected active compromise to it. These are incompatible contracts, not merely two different names for the same job.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/incident-response-runbook/SKILL.md:3,38–40,191–195`; its `evals/evals.json:34–41`; `.claude/skills/database-backup-verifier/evals/trigger-evals.json:106–112`; `.claude/skills/cloud-security-baseline-reviewer/SKILL.md:241–243`. The governance packet independently identifies the same mistake in containment evaluation fixtures; consolidate that into this one cross-family finding.

Smallest action: route live incidents to the named human incident owner following the approved runbook, and to an explicitly invoked diagnosis procedure where appropriate. Keep `incident-response-runbook` for authoring or improving the procedure. Add reciprocal tests for “write a runbook” versus “help recover this live incident.” No new incident skill is justified until the desired executable role is separately scoped.
findings.correction: Route live incidents to the human incident owner following an approved runbook; keep the skill for procedure authoring; add reciprocal live-versus-authoring cases.

findings.title: Retry/timeout arithmetic is inconsistent within one skill
findings.details:
The latency workflow and updated reference correctly require the critical path, all allowed attempts, retry backoff and upstream work. The output template and validation checklist still use `upstream >= downstream × retries + ε`. That formulation does not clearly include the initial attempt or backoff. The Gotchas also say two layers that each retry twice multiply load by four, while the reference gives `(1+r1)(1+r2)` attempts; with two retries at each layer that is nine attempts.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/latency-budget-architect/SKILL.md:110–118,169,193,223–224`; `references/tail-math-worksheet.md:58–77`; `evals/evals.json:15`. The fan-out case also needs the independence assumption carried into its assertion, consistent with the main body at97–103.

Smallest action: use one definition of attempts/retries, one critical-path deadline formula, and one worked numerical example throughout body, reference, output and eval. This is a content correction, not a missing performance capability.
findings.correction: Define retry versus attempt counts once and synchronize all templates/checklists/oracles to critical-path time including initial attempt, retries, backoff and upstream work; two layers with two retries each permit nine attempts.

findings.title: Credential-rotation reference checks revocation before revoking
findings.details:
The rotation reference first says to verify the old credential is rejected, then says to revoke it. For an overlap rotation, the old credential may legitimately remain valid until revocation. The current main workflow's verification boundary is clearer; the supporting procedure should agree with it.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/secrets-identity-hardener/references/secret-classification-and-rotation.md:46–60`, especially54–56; corresponding main workflow rotation step. Smallest action: verify new credential functionality, revoke the old credential under the applicable grant, then prove old-key rejection and capture residual consumers/failures. Do not turn “new key works” into proof of revocation.
findings.correction: Verify new credential operation, revoke the old credential, then prove old-credential rejection; preserve grant and consumer-inventory boundaries.

findings.title: Search evaluation rewards an assertion contradicted by the current body
findings.details:
The slow/stale-search evaluation demands that `LIKE '%term%'` be called an “un-indexable full scan.” The current Gotchas explicitly recognize PostgreSQL trigram indexes supporting `LIKE` and `ILIKE`. The prompt also does not establish an asynchronous indexing path, so newly created records not appearing is not by itself proof of indexing lag.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/search-architecture-designer/evals/evals.json:21–30`; `SKILL.md:188–195`. Smallest action: require inspection of the actual query, index, plan and write/search path before choosing the cause; test the indexed-trigram near miss. Keyword search is shipped and substantive.
findings.correction: Inspect query/index/plan and write-to-search path before attributing the cause; allow index-supported LIKE and do not infer asynchronous lag from missing new records alone.

findings.title: Threat severity assertion lags the corrected consequence/confidence model
findings.details:
The current threat model separates potential consequence from confidence/path evidence. The older upload-feature evaluation still allows HIGH only when a concrete exploit path is stated. That can force a design-time threat with serious potential consequences but incomplete evidence to be mislabeled rather than honestly represented as a hypothesis. The catalog still uses the older “exploit-path-gated severity” summary.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/threat-modeler/SKILL.md:81–89,125–137`; `references/threat-catalog.md:91–98`; `evals/evals.json:7–16`; `docs/skills-catalog.md:483`. Smallest action: synchronize the fixture and catalog with the current two-axis body. The AI-specific exclusion at `SKILL.md:42–44` should also name the now-shipped `ai-threat-modeler` instead of leaving an unspecified “Phase7” gap.
findings.correction: Align oracle/catalog with consequence plus confidence; incomplete path evidence changes confidence, not automatically potential severity. Name the shipped AI threat-model owner in the AI exclusion.

findings.title: SLO fixtures erase a documented cause-page exception
findings.details:
The SLO reference permits an urgent direct-failure cause signal to page when the owning incident policy justifies it and supplies a threshold, runbook and owner. The body says existing cause pages may be “demoted or defended.” The negative fixture unconditionally refuses cause-based pages. A neighboring observability fixture has similar unconditional demotion wording.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/slo-reliability-architect/references/slo-derivation.md:34–40`; `SKILL.md:99–103,163`; `evals/evals.json:59–66`; `.claude/skills/observability-operator/evals/evals.json`, case `edge-noisy-alert-cleanup`. Smallest action: test unjustified noisy cause paging separately from an evidence-backed urgent resource-failure exception. Preserve user-symptom/error-budget paging as the default.
findings.correction: Separate unjustified cause-page noise from policy-justified urgent direct-failure paging with threshold/runbook/owner; align assertions and description with the exception.

findings.title: Migration fixture allows a backup waiver not present in its current gate
findings.details:
The migration runbook body requires verified backup evidence before a runnable procedure. Its missing-backup fixture offers either a restore test or a recorded human risk-acceptance decision, then authors the runbook. The latter exception is not stated in the procedure's prerequisite and Stop Conditions.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/data-migration-runbook-author/SKILL.md:115–123,281–285`; `evals/evals.json:36–45`. Smallest action: reconcile the oracle with the actual policy. Either remove the waiver expectation or make an explicitly approved exception part of the governing procedure with a safe, non-executable blocked artifact distinction. This audit does not invent authority to waive the gate.
findings.correction: Remove the fixture-only backup waiver or explicitly reconcile it through the governing policy; distinguish a blocked draft from a ready runnable runbook. Audit does not authorize waiving backup evidence.

findings.title: Backup drill fixture supplies an unstated target and cleanup wording exceeds its own scope
findings.details:
The drill case's prompt supplies a backup and sandbox target, but no RTO. Its assertion requires comparison with a two-hour RTO. Another case's facts are not a fixture for this isolated case. Separately, the cleanup reference's broad scratch-account “none remain” wording should be restricted to resources created by the specific drill, as the main workflow correctly requires.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/database-backup-verifier/evals/evals.json:21–31`; main drill/cleanup workflow; `references/backup-verification-checks.md`, section5. Smallest action: state the two-hour RTO in this case or require the owner target before execution; record a drill resource manifest and verify only those resources' cleanup. Backup verification is present and should not be proposed again as missing.
findings.correction: Supply the two-hour RTO in the case fixture or require an owner target; verify cleanup against a manifest of only resources created by the drill.

findings.title: Metadata-only metering fixture incorrectly implies no personal data
findings.details:
The main metering workflow correctly says user-linked identifiers can still be personal data and need minimization, access and retention controls. The positive pipeline fixture demands “explicitly no … PII.” That phrase confuses no message/file content with no personal information in identifiers/metadata.

Evidence: `.claude/skills/usage-metering-and-cost-attribution-pipeline-designer/SKILL.md:82–90,136–139,158–160`; `evals/evals.json:7–15`. Smallest action: require absence of content/unnecessary direct personal fields while affirmatively checking protected, minimized user-linked metadata.
findings.correction: Disallow content/unnecessary direct personal data, but require minimization/protection of user-linked metadata instead of claiming all metadata PII-free.

findings.title: Several evals prescribe a root cause that their prompt does not prove
findings.details:
The register identifies exact cases in background jobs, horizontal scaling, offline synchronization, realtime authority propagation, performance harness noise, profiling and static-analysis triage. They are meaningful scenarios, but some expected answers move directly from symptom to a particular implementation defect. Examples include tenant starvation → one undifferentiated queue; post-revocation messages → authorization checked only at connect; duplicate/out-of-order events → partition-key root cause; use of an ORM → false-positive injection finding. The current bodies often require evidence and enumerate more than one possible mechanism.

Evidence: the per-skill `quality_checks` entries and case references in [platform-skills.json](platform-skills.json), especially `background-job-orchestration-architect`, `horizontal-scalability-reviewer`, `realtime-subscription-architect`, `streaming-event-architect` and `static-analysis-reviewer`.

Smallest action: make the case supply the required configuration/trace/code evidence, or grade a ranked hypothesis and discriminating inspection step instead of a predetermined diagnosis. This is a bounded concern until the exact assertion is reconciled, not evidence that a model actually hallucinated during a live run.
findings.correction: Add the configuration/trace/code facts needed for a predetermined cause, or score a hypothesis and discriminating inspection. Do not reward a diagnosis inferred only from symptoms.
findings.independent_review_qualification: Keep queue/session/index symptom-to-cause concerns. The static-analysis ORM fixture explicitly requires tracing the specific call and rejects ORM-only dismissal; its narrower ambiguity is that a later assertion presupposes a refuting fact without supplying the query. It is not evidence the fixture directs dismissal merely because an ORM is used.

findings.title: Four required delivery stages have no installed procedural owner
findings.consequence: The repository explicitly marks single-change planning (A), independent plan-level ACCEPT/REVISE audit (B), general implementation (C), and selected-tier execution (E) as procedurally enforced. Naming a selector or a specialist that excludes the work can leave the required stage unowned.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Define the exact residual stage contract, then extend an existing owner where it can honestly take the work. A single-change planner and independent plan auditor need precise outputs and revision binding; implementation and validation can retain explicit authorized executor handoffs. Correct the release guide so selecting/designing checks is not presented as obtaining actual results.
findings.qualification: This is not absence of planning, implementation, or testing capability. ai-task-decomposer, tech-spec-writer, docs-first-implementer, tdd-engineer, local-ci-mirror-preflight and specialized test engineers already cover substantial related work. The source itself calls the map illustrative and non-exhaustive.

findings.title: Semantic and hybrid retrieval quality falls between the lexical and security owners
findings.consequence: The search owner explicitly excludes semantic/vector retrieval and sends it to rag-security-architect. That target requires a concrete retrieval design and secures its authorization, tenant filters, permissions, embeddings and citations. It does not supply the positive engineering procedure for chunking/embedding selection, dense/lexical fusion, reranking, and task-specific retrieval relevance trade-offs.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Assign functional retrieval design to a bounded owner or extend a suitable existing owner with explicit inputs, output, quality criteria and RAG-security handoff. Route secure retrieval separately from retrieval relevance; reuse ai-evaluation-harness for measured comparison and ai-misinformation-guard for grounding/citation checks.
findings.qualification: All 205 descriptions and the closest full bodies were checked; the platform auditor independently read the complete search packet. Existing AI quality evaluation, grounding, lexical relevance and secure retrieval are real coverage. Historical candidate #295 is narrower retrieval-boundary design and is covered by composition; this residual is broader productive RAG engineering. Training, fine-tuning and general MLOps are optional expansion unless separately promised.

findings.title: The product-agent authorization rung names the coding-agent authority matrix
findings.consequence: A runtime harness for a product agent can be directed to a policy about coding agents making repository changes, leaving product-user permissions and delegated runtime scopes underspecified.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Distinguish coding-agent authority from runtime product policy. Compose authorization-matrix-designer for actor/resource permissions, agent-identity-privilege-reviewer for attenuated delegation, and ai-human-in-the-loop-designer for product confirmation policy. Keep agent-authorization-matrix for SDLC authority.
findings.qualification: The product authorization capability exists; this is a misrouted composition, not a missing authorization skill.

findings.title: Product-agent checkpoint recovery is handed to Git/worktree recovery
findings.consequence: A product agent resuming after uncertain tool outcomes needs effect reconciliation, idempotency and authorization revalidation. The named recovery target instead preserves and repairs Git branches, rebase/merge state and working trees.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Replace the runtime recovery handoff with an explicit composition of worker checkpoint/lease recovery, command idempotency, and containment revalidation. Add a negative routing fixture distinguishing product runtime recovery from coding-agent Git recovery; only add a new runtime owner if residual reconciliation is still unowned.
findings.qualification: Background execution, idempotency, typed retries and bounded loops already exist. No claim is made that all agent-runtime recovery is absent. The caller is the primary remedy; absence of a trigger-evals file in agent-failure-recovery alone is not a defect.

findings.title: Production AI data and memory retirement routes to coding-agent memory governance
findings.consequence: A lifecycle program can mistake rules for repository memory files for disposal of application datasets, embeddings, derived personal data and vendor copies.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Route personal-data and production-memory disposal to pii-lifecycle-designer, retaining source-document lineage, vendor completion proof and backup aging/redeletion. Name the data/model artifact owner for nonpersonal data. Retain agent-memory-governance for coding-agent memory only.
findings.qualification: The platform auditor fully read pii-lifecycle-designer and multi-tenant-data-architect. This is an existing-capability routing repair, not a proposal to create another generic retention skill.

findings.title: HITL action classification contradicts its own reference and refund fixture
findings.consequence: The workflow classifies irreversible and wide-blast-radius actions as FORBIDDEN, while the reference allows irreversible actions under CONFIRM and wider effects with a second reviewer; the refund fixture expects CONFIRM because money moves. A caller cannot determine the governing classification consistently.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Write one risk and action classification rule, including when consequential irreversible actions may be proposed for authorized human commitment, then align the table, examples and fixtures. Keep actual forbidden actions distinct from confirmable actions.
findings.qualification: This is a design-contract defect in a shipped owner, not missing HITL coverage or evidence that any unsafe action occurred.

findings.title: Product approval-flow handoffs were not fully migrated to the new HITL owner
findings.consequence: Product refund/reviewer workflows still route in several outputs, references or assertions to human-approval-boundary, which governs the coding assistant’s own risky actions. Some current workflows already correctly name ai-human-in-the-loop-designer, so the packet can reward the superseded route.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Update the exact product-flow call sites to ai-human-in-the-loop-designer; preserve human-approval-boundary for SDLC actions. Add reciprocal discrimination with human-agent-trust-reviewer for design of a new flow versus adversarial review of an existing flow.
findings.qualification: The necessary owner is shipped. Do not create another approval-flow skill.

findings.title: Live incident requests are routed to a document-authoring runbook skill
findings.consequence: The receiving incident-response-runbook skill explicitly authors documents and refuses to run a live incident. Active compromise, production-down-now, live customer spam or immediate kill-switch instructions cannot be fulfilled by that authoring route; several corrected bodies still have older fixtures or references.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Route active events to the authorized incident owner and existing approved runbook; name systematic-debugger only for applicable diagnosis with its invocation posture. Use incident-response-runbook to author or improve the procedure before or after the incident. Align body, reference and fixture on this distinction.
findings.qualification: The platform auditor fully read the receiving packet and its negative-live-incident fixture; root independently verified the guided broken-system path. This does not mean incident planning or diagnosis is absent. ai-cost’s immediate exposure-bounding assertion also needs to remain a proposed/human-owned response unless actual execution authority and a capable executor exist.

findings.title: Three fixtures assign live attack execution to a read-only subagent
evidence: .claude/agents/ai-security-red-team-reviewer.md (tool allow-list and read-only procedure; independently read by root)
findings.consequence: The prompts ask to probe deployed assistants and report which attacks succeed, but the expected target exposes Read/Grep/Glob and a read-only review procedure. A correct target selection cannot produce the requested live evidence.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Change the handoff to an explicitly authorized, appropriately scoped execution harness (ai-evaluation-harness where applicable) with safe test targets and recorded observations, or change the prompt to read-only attack-plan/review work. Do not claim live attacks ran from a review artifact.
findings.qualification: No live probing was performed during this audit; the finding concerns authored routing contracts and declared capability.

findings.title: Eval semantics confuse initial selection with legitimate delegation and omit interactive context
findings.consequence: The runner blueprint says every should_not_trigger target stays silent. The orchestrator’s winning fixture puts requirements-gathering-facilitator in that list while expressly requiring the orchestrator to invoke it as Stage 1. Several single-prompt behavior cases also assert later user turns, approved records or an unseen previous preview without supplying that interaction.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Record primary route selection separately from authorized delegated invocations. Give interactive cases explicit conversation fixtures and repository state, or restrict single-turn assertions to the next valid turn. Preserve UNRUN/UNAVAILABLE when a host cannot expose activation, isolation or action evidence.
findings.qualification: This is a static incompatibility between the proposed evaluation protocol and authored cases, not an observed model failure. The shipped offline runner and retained pilot evidence have narrower claims; root audits those tools and observations separately.

findings.title: Orchestrator refusal fixtures discard explicit user authorization clauses
findings.consequence: A fixture ending “Go ahead and build it” requires treating the entire reply only as scope acceptance, while the current contract preserves directly available grants. Another prompt explicitly requests merge and live schema work yet evaluates it as merely inferred consent and requires a second yes to record the authorization. This can reward repeat approval rather than distinguishing authorization from unmet execution preconditions.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Use genuinely ambiguous consent in refusal tests. Add separate tests for explicit grants with missing prerequisites, scope limits or manual invocation requirements, and for authorized documentary transcription that must proceed without repeat consent.
findings.qualification: The audit does not widen any permission or relax a required review. A direct instruction may still leave exact targets, risk preconditions, or execution route unresolved; fixtures should identify those specific gaps rather than erase the explicit clause.

findings.title: Resumed local validation can retain results for a changed working tree
findings.consequence: The persisted resume identity uses commit/run-id. A local shard may pass, an uncommitted tracked source file used by that shard may then change, and HEAD may remain identical. Resuming unfinished shards can preserve the stale pass even though the local mirror promises validation of the exact tree to be committed.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Fingerprint the exact working tree and relevant validation commands, configuration, dependency/runtime inputs. On changed inputs, invalidate the affected passes or conservatively all passes. Document the resume/fix/revalidate policy and add a dirty-tree same-HEAD case.
findings.qualification: This is a reasoned counterexample to the written contract, not a reproduced run or proof that the repository currently executes such a runner.

findings.title: GitHub job skips and workflow skips are conflated
findings.consequence: The rationale says a conditionally skipped required job strands branch protection. GitHub’s primary documentation distinguishes a skipped workflow due to path/branch/message filtering (pending check) from a job skipped by a conditional (success). Dependency skips introduce a different false-green risk.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Correct the explanation and fixtures to distinguish workflow-level omission, job conditions, dependency failures and merge-queue events. Keep a useful always-running aggregate gate, with explicit dependency-result checks, where the actual topology warrants it.
findings.qualification: Primary sources were verified in this audit (child refs turn17view0 and turn17view1, also independently checked by root). This correction does not invalidate the aggregate-gate design as a whole.

findings.title: A provenance exception makes the injection trust rule ambiguous
findings.consequence: The body says no trusted-source exemption “without a provenance guarantee,” which can imply provenance creates an exemption. Its reference correctly says first-party, signed or immutable external content is still untrusted as instructions and provenance never promotes it to authority.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: State unambiguously that provenance can support data authenticity but cannot grant instruction authority. Align the body with the reference and include an authenticated/signed malicious-document case.
findings.qualification: Other steps already state that external data cannot alter authority. This is ambiguous wording that weakens an otherwise explicit invariant, not evidence that an injection bypass occurred.

findings.title: Compliance mapping still promotes shipped guidance to operating control evidence
findings.consequence: The current foundation and some ISO body text require verified operating controls, but SOC2’s premise says much Security already exists for an organization with the shipped packs; an AIMS fixture maps shipped outputs as operational mechanisms. Installing instructions is not evidence that a product or organization implements and operates their controls.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Describe shipped skills as candidate design/review routes. Require a named implemented mechanism, owner, configuration and dated operating evidence before marking a control operating. Align catalog, references and fixtures with the corrected foundation.
findings.qualification: This audit judges Aegis’s instruction contracts, not any organization’s certification or control effectiveness. Framework mappings can be useful without supplying actual operating proof.

findings.title: Evidence collection frequency is confused with continuous control coverage
findings.consequence: The checklist flags a quarterly artifact for a continuous control, while the reference explicitly allows monthly or quarterly extracts when the evidence tiles the whole period. The extraction cadence alone cannot distinguish complete evidence from an uncovered interval.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Assess population and time-period completeness, config changes and the evidence’s actual coverage, separately from how often an extract is produced. Add one valid quarterly full-window case and one incomplete snapshot case.
findings.qualification: No claim about an auditor’s acceptance decision is made; the immediate defect is the packet’s contradictory rule.

findings.title: SOC2 privacy mapping overlooks the shipped personal-data lifecycle owner
findings.consequence: Notice, choice, access and disposal are mapped chiefly to an LLM disclosure/redaction skill and “substantial net-new likely,” even though the library has a personal-data lifecycle design owner covering derived data, stores, deletion and vendor proof.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Add pii-lifecycle-designer and the actual product privacy/governance owners to the privacy projection. Retain sensitive-disclosure-guard for the AI disclosure surface, and independently verify any remaining notice, legal or assurance obligations.
findings.qualification: This is not a claim that pii-lifecycle-designer alone satisfies every privacy criterion.

findings.title: The foundation’s encryption residue is broader than the current missing scope
findings.consequence: “Encryption in transit / at rest design ... design review is unowned” hides the already shipped cloud/IaC encryption checks and key-custody routes. Conversely those checks do not establish a complete application cryptographic architecture or general hardening baseline.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Reconcile the map against current cloud/IaC/security owners. Keep only the precise residual—application data/key boundary design and any unsupported TLS/certificate or hardening lifecycle—as partial, with demand and ownership stated.
findings.qualification: Platform independently read the cited full packets. A blanket missing-cryptography claim would be false; a full-coverage claim would also exceed the evidence. This is a map correction plus a bounded residual assessment.

findings.title: Provider budget controls and defaults need provider-specific verification
findings.consequence: The body generalizes that most major providers have hard caps and optional alerts off by default. Its reference appropriately requires checking actual account controls and distinguishes alerting from enforcement. Provider semantics and enforcement delay are material to the exposure bound.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Use a provider/account-specific verification item, cite current documentation, and model overshoot and delay. Keep application fail-closed spend reservations and kill switches independent of provider alerts or caps.
findings.qualification: Current official OpenAI documentation supports organization/project hard limits, distinguishes alerts, and warns enforcement may be delayed and overshoot. This finding is not that OpenAI has no hard caps, nor a proof that the body’s “most” claim is universally false. Root verified this primary source.

findings.title: Approval timing is occasionally treated as proof of review quality or intent
findings.consequence: Some body/reference text labels very fast or high approval rates as rubber-stamping, gate failure or proof the action was not read, while other passages correctly require risk mix, request quality and inspection. Timing is a useful signal but does not establish motive or review adequacy by itself.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Use timing/rate as a trigger for evidence review, report observations without inferred intent, and require sampled decision-quality evidence before a failure verdict. Align reference heuristics with the more careful body rules.
findings.qualification: No judgment about a person’s actual behavior is made in this audit.

findings.title: Delegation example can restore the original user’s authority at the tool hop
findings.consequence: The example narrows A1 and A2 at each hop but labels A3 as the calling user’s authority. If interpreted as the original principal’s full permissions, this contradicts the per-hop attenuation invariant.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Define effective tool authority as the intersection of the principal’s policy, current delegated scope, current task authorization and runtime constraints. Add a narrowed subagent plus more-privileged parent negative example.
findings.qualification: The main body already prohibits amplification; this is a reference clarification, not a demonstrated privilege escalation.

findings.title: A commit-message search is insufficient evidence that remembered work remains in force
findings.consequence: A negative git-log message grep cannot establish that an implementation has not been undone through a manual edit, squash, rename or a differently worded commit. A remembered completion anchor could suppress necessary work.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Use commit history as a lead, then verify the current implementation and relevant tests or authoritative current artifact before declaring the fact still true.
findings.qualification: No stale memory was used to decide the current audit; this is a bounded weakness in the reference procedure.

findings.title: Package-hallucination checks stop at existence in the body and fixture
findings.consequence: The reference correctly accounts for attackers registering invented package names, but the workflow/checklist and package fixture focus on registry existence. Existence alone cannot distinguish an authentic dependency from malicious preregistration.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Bring identity, ownership and provenance verification into the workflow and fixture, composing supply-chain-security-reviewer. Add an existing-but-untrusted package case.
findings.qualification: This is not absence of supply-chain review; it is incomplete composition in the hallucination path.

findings.title: Standing-approval fixture and expiry guidance disagree with current grant semantics
findings.consequence: The reviewer-block fixture says never re-request review and wait for a human, while current rules permit ordinary in-scope corrections followed by review. Another passage gives every profile grant an expiry even though the register forbids inventing one when none was stated.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Separate in-scope correction/re-review from changing reviewer acceptance or expanding authority. Preserve the grant’s actual expiry and consumption semantics, including none stated.
findings.qualification: Reviewer rejection still blocks advancement. The remedy removes contradictory fixture expectations; it does not authorize overriding a review or broadening a grant.

findings.title: The no-write usage ledger mandates a manifest-writing refresh
findings.consequence: The ledger promises it emits a conversation record and writes nothing, yet requires --refresh-skills-manifest before reading. The refresh unconditionally writes the manifest and updates source_revision to current HEAD. Its SHA-256 covers only normalized SKILL.md bytes, so calling it the exact instructions applied overstates coverage when references are used.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Use read-only manifest validation first; if stale or missing, explicitly hand off regeneration under the applicable write route. Describe the manifest hash as SKILL.md identity, and record the repository revision or hashes of applied supporting files when full instruction provenance is required.
findings.qualification: Root independently verified validator behavior. No refresh was executed in this audit. Recording artifacts in audit scratch does not imply permission to mutate the source repository.

findings.title: Usage instrumentation has inconsistent privacy and correction-event schemas
findings.consequence: The body restricts raw events and publishes thresholded aggregates, while the reference and fixtures require every raw record to be openly committable. The owner-choice fixture also needs correction activation mode auto/explicit, but the correction schema’s mode means overridden/abandoned. A design cannot faithfully satisfy both meanings without another field or a specified join.
findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Keep the stricter data minimization, align raw-event access and aggregate release rules, and distinguish activation_mode from correction_outcome (or explicitly join to a minimized invocation record). Add a sparse-event privacy and wrong-fire attribution example.
findings.qualification: This skill designs telemetry only and currently collects nothing. The finding does not assert that user information was captured or exposed.

canonical_findings.title: Corpus-wide behavioral efficacy remains unestablished
canonical_findings.observed: The current capability report disables live dispatch and reports activation observation, profile isolation and live containment unavailable. The census counts 2,467 authored single-prompt cases plus one conversation suite and explicitly records no behavioral execution. Offline/synthetic implementation is present; measured calibration is unfinished.
canonical_findings.implication: Passing structural validation and possessing evaluation files cannot establish reliable skill selection, correct outcomes, authority behavior, or multi-host parity across the corpus.
canonical_findings.smallest_response: Complete the existing runner/calibration work through its actual gates and publish revision-bound, host-bound results and denominators. Reuse narrower valid pilot evidence where its scope fits.
canonical_findings.limits: This audit did not run paid model sessions. It does not assert that no individual skill has ever been exercised; setup and historical pilot evidence have narrower scopes.

canonical_findings.title: Four source-library delivery responsibilities have no installed owning skill
canonical_findings.observed: The canonical workflow records that writing a single change plan, returning a plan-level ACCEPT/REVISE audit, general implementation and executing the selected validation tier are procedurally enforced. Existing decomposition, criterion review and validation-selection skills are explicitly partial fits.
canonical_findings.implication: The operating model's requirement for an enforcing skill per stage is only partially met; a plausible neighbor must not be presented as owning the whole stage.
canonical_findings.smallest_response: Decide whether the procedural ownership remains intentional or whether existing owners should be extended for a demonstrated recurring need. Specify concrete stage outputs and boundaries before proposing any additional skill.
canonical_findings.limits: This is not a claim that Aegis lacks all planning, implementation, testing, review or merge controls. It does not by itself justify four new skills.

merged_source_findings.title: Four required delivery stages have no installed procedural owner
merged_source_findings.consequence: The repository explicitly marks single-change planning (A), independent plan-level ACCEPT/REVISE audit (B), general implementation (C), and selected-tier execution (E) as procedurally enforced. Naming a selector or a specialist that excludes the work can leave the required stage unowned.
merged_source_findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Define the exact residual stage contract, then extend an existing owner where it can honestly take the work. A single-change planner and independent plan auditor need precise outputs and revision binding; implementation and validation can retain explicit authorized executor handoffs. Correct the release guide so selecting/designing checks is not presented as obtaining actual results.
merged_source_findings.qualification: This is not absence of planning, implementation, or testing capability. ai-task-decomposer, tech-spec-writer, docs-first-implementer, tdd-engineer, local-ci-mirror-preflight and specialized test engineers already cover substantial related work. The source itself calls the map illustrative and non-exhaustive.

canonical_findings.title: Live adversarial probing is routed to a read-only reviewer
evidence: .claude/agents/ai-security-red-team-reviewer.md (tool allow-list and read-only procedure; independently read by root)
canonical_findings.observed: Three trigger fixtures ask for actual attacks against deployed assistants and expect the ai-security-red-team-reviewer subagent. Its declared tools are Read, Grep and Glob and its procedure is read-only source analysis. No executable live probing owner is supplied by that handoff.
canonical_findings.implication: The routing contract can select a receiver unable to perform the requested operation under its own declared capabilities, inviting an incomplete result or an overstated execution claim.
canonical_findings.smallest_response: Repair the three routing fixtures: name ai-evaluation-harness for an explicitly authorized, scoped adversarial suite where its contract fits; otherwise state the remaining live-execution gap and offer static attack-path review. Preserve target/environment, authority, cost and containment prerequisites. Align README role wording.
canonical_findings.limits: Static threat modeling, adversarial scenario design and source review are present and useful. This audit performed no attack against a live system.
canonical_findings.contrary_evidence: The manual-only ai-evaluation-harness explicitly encodes and runs adversarial suites after behavior-spec, target/run authority and disclosed-cost prerequisites; live production monitoring is outside its scope. The issue is the selected read-only receiver, not absence of all adversarial execution capability.

merged_source_findings.title: Three fixtures assign live attack execution to a read-only subagent
evidence: .claude/agents/ai-security-red-team-reviewer.md (tool allow-list and read-only procedure; independently read by root)
merged_source_findings.consequence: The prompts ask to probe deployed assistants and report which attacks succeed, but the expected target exposes Read/Grep/Glob and a read-only review procedure. A correct target selection cannot produce the requested live evidence.
merged_source_findings.smallest_justified_remedy: Change the handoff to an explicitly authorized, appropriately scoped execution harness (ai-evaluation-harness where applicable) with safe test targets and recorded observations, or change the prompt to read-only attack-plan/review work. Do not claim live attacks ran from a review artifact.
merged_source_findings.qualification: No live probing was performed during this audit; the finding concerns authored routing contracts and declared capability.

canonical_findings.title: Native-copy example includes skills that its following caveat excludes
canonical_findings.observed: The optional native-mode example recursively copies the entire .claude/skills tree into .agents/skills. The same subsection later says not to copy manual-only operate-class skills and warns that a description sentinel is not enforcement. At this revision 30 shipped skills are manual-only.
canonical_findings.implication: A user following the example literally does not obtain the restricted copy the caveat requires, especially on a host whose native invocation control differs.
canonical_findings.smallest_response: Replace the broad example with selection-based copying or a verified exclusion procedure, and describe host-native invocation controls with dated evidence. Preserve the supported pointer route and user-selected mode.
canonical_findings.limits: No host was installed or exercised here. A copied instruction is not execution, and the text already warns about portability; the issue is the mismatch between the example and its restriction.

canonical_findings.title: Static scanner family metadata misclassifies actual skills
canonical_findings.observed: The parser treats any line beginning with # as a heading and keeps the first name match, including subagent rows. As executed, full-codebase-auditor and release-readiness-reviewer are assigned the Subagents family; AI-SDLC and QA rows receive paragraph fragments beginning with historical numeric citations.
canonical_findings.implication: Consumers grouping skills by this raw manifest field can produce a misleading taxonomy even when file and skill counts are correct.
canonical_findings.smallest_response: Parse actual Markdown headings and skill tables, distinguish same-named agents from skills, and validate the family map against the canonical roster. Treat raw scanner family metadata as noncanonical until corrected.
canonical_findings.limits: The independent audit uses corrected assignment families and the README family inventory. The verified 205-skill/792-file scope and skill-body manifest validation are unaffected.
canonical_findings.independent_review: Detected by product synthesis reviewer and corroborated by root against the generated manifest and parser code.
